subject: Downstream attribution & model-consent routing — MSA / Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Janet Morris <jmorris@finos.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Huang <d.huang@finos.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redlines to MSA — output handling and retrain consent

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Our legal team ran through the MSA + Order Form and attached a redline with three areas they asked us to flag for more explicit language:

- Downstream attribution and productization (they want language to ensure FinOS receives notice and attribution if Redwood productizes outputs derived from FinOS prompts)
- Retrain consent / opt-in (suggested an explicit opt-in clause for any model retraining that uses FinOS data or outputs)
- Feedback license scope (limits on using customer-provided prompts, labels and telemetry)

I've attached FinOS_MSA_redline_v3.docx with inline comments. We want to keep momentum—can you route this to your legal and product teams and let us know which items are negotiable vs deal blockers?

Also looping Daniel (product) for any technical constraints.

Thanks,
Janet Morris
Legal Counsel | FinOS
Attachments: FinOS_MSA_redline_v3.docx (Word document)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA — output handling and retrain consent

Janet — appreciate the clear summary and the redline.

Quick initial thoughts:
- We agree on the need for clarity; some of the FinOS language as written is broader than our standard product commitments (particularly the attribution clause).
- Retrain opt-in: operationally we support opt-in for any customer data used for model updates. We need the clause to reflect the mechanics (e.g., how customers give consent, embargo windows, and minimum notice).
- Feedback license: we typically request a non-exclusive, royalty-free feedback license limited to model quality and safety improvements. Full rights to reuse customer outputs for productization is a heavier ask for us.

Laura — can you review the attached doc and propose counter-text for each of the three areas above? Ben — please flag any product/ops impacts if we accept narrower or broader language. Irene — can you prepare a suggested negotiable map and the HubSpot playbook entry so we can push this through the commercial thread quickly?

Janet — we'll come back with redline-counter and a short summary of impacts by EOD Tuesday PDT. If any of these items are immediate blockers from FinOS's side, call that out.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Janet Morris <jmorris@finos.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA — output handling and retrain consent

Monica / team / Janet — attaching my annotated counter-proposal and a one-page memo that maps each FinOS ask to risk and suggested language. Highlights: 

1) Downstream attribution / productization
- FinOS text: Customers must be notified and attributed if Redwood productizes derivative outputs.
- Our risk: The term "productize" is vague and could be interpreted to require attribution for routine model improvements or anonymized features.
- Proposed language: We offer to include a notice-and-consent trigger for explicit product launches that materially derive from FinOS-provided content. We define a conservative materiality threshold and a 30-day notice period.

2) Retrain consent / opt-in
- Proposed operational clause: Any retrain that includes FinOS data or outputs will require explicit written opt-in (checkbox via Console or signed amendment). We propose a 60-day embargo before any retrain using customer data goes into production, and the customer may opt-out at any time for future retrains.

3) Feedback license scope
- We accept a limited feedback license for model improvement, safety research, and debugging. We will not assert ownership over FinOS-originated content or grant rights for FinOS-originated outputs to be sold or sublicensed.

Document: redline-consolidation-notes.xlsx (summary of clauses) attached.

Action items: Monica/Irene please confirm whether the 30/60-day windows meet the commercial timeline. Janet — if FinOS needs faster timelines, indicate which items are have-to-have vs nice-to-have.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline-consolidation-notes.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Janet Morris <jmorris@finos.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA — output handling and retrain consent

Quick product/ops note — thanks for the clear framing Laura. A couple of technical realities to surface: 

- Materiality detection: determining whether a new product "materially derives" from FinOS prompts may require human review in ambiguous cases. That adds latency; we should bake in a decision SLA (e.g., our team will assess within 7 business days).
- Embargo mechanics: a 60-day embargo is workable but we should define what "retrain" means (full model retrain vs micro-updates / continual learning). I suggest the clause call out "production model weights" changes as the trigger.
- Audit trail: to honor the opt-in/opt-out, we need to persist consent flags and attach them to dataset snapshots. That has minor storage/retention implications — estimate +2% infra cost for the first year for this deal.

If FinOS insists on real-time productization attribution, we should consider an alternate commercial credit (discount / data token) rather than operational guarantees.

Happy to walk FinOS through the practical implementation next week.

Ben Carter
Head of Product | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA — output handling and retrain consent

Janet / Monica — quick commercial proposal to keep the deal moving: 

1) We accept Laura's proposed language with the 30-day notice and 60-day retrain embargo.
2) We will commit to a 7-business-day materiality review SLA for disputed cases.
3) For attribution on productized features, Redwood will provide reasonable attribution where productization is directly dependent on FinOS outputs. For broader product features, we'll provide a commercial credit of 4% ARR against the first-year committed spend instead of a blanket attribution guarantee.

Janet — is FinOS open to the 4% credit in lieu of hard attribution? If yes, we can incorporate the concession into the order form and circulate a final redline for signature. HubSpot deal is updated here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

I'll also open a DocuSign envelope once we have final language: https://docusign.com/FinOS-RDW-MSAv3

Thanks,
Irene Choi
